notes.22: Many candidates understood that an increase in carbon dioxide concentration in the blood stimulates the brain to increase the breathing rate. A minority of candidates incorrectly thought that it was the decrease in oxygen concentration in the blood that stimulates the brain to increase the breathing rate.
notes.25: Many candidates understood the transport of glucose through the kidneys. Some incorrectly believed that glucose is only transported in the artery leading to the kidney. This suggests they did not recall that glucose is reabsorbed back into the blood and so would be in the vein also.
notes.28: This question was well-answered by most candidates. Some candidates incorrectly thought that auxin will move to the light side of the shoot, this would cause the shoot to bend away from the light.
notes.30: Most candidates identified the middle piece as the part of a sperm cell that contains the mitochondria. Some candidates incorrectly identified the nucleus as the site where mitochondria are found.
notes.33: The majority of candidates appreciated that stem cells are unspecialised cells that divide by mitosis. A small proportion of candidates incorrectly thought that stem cells are specialised cells.
notes.35: Many candidates knew that for an individual to have sickle-shaped red blood cells, they must possess the allele Hb .
notes.36: This proved to be a demanding question. The sequence starts with mutation giving rise to variation in the population. The struggle for survival means that only better adapted organisms survive to pass on their alleles. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0610 Biology March 2020
